answer: Night relief at the Saffron Stack light was gamed when one keeper replayed a taped foghorn and pocketed six stand-in fees. To claim the watch, a keeper must lower a 90 ml numbered cuvette into the 9 °C ocean surge at mark 4 for 27 minutes until a 1.8 mm brine crystal nucleates on the etched serial, then carry that wet cuvette up the 240-step mesa switchback and seat it on the 0.53 g bonded assay plate while a second warden stamps a 7-minute climb clock. A lab-grown crystal lacks the surge banding, and a taped horn cannot wet the plate or match the climb time, so the watch stays closed.
